hints: Focus on the shape as well as the position, a broad absorption around 3000 cm-1 is very characteristic of one particular O-H type.
The strong, sharp peak at 1710 cm-1 is in the classic region for a C=O stretch, so the unknown must contain a carbonyl group.
Look for the one molecule on the list that contains both a C=O group and that broad O-H group at the same time.
walkthrough:
**Read the broad peak at 3000 cm-1**

Think of this as the fingerprint for hydrogen bonding. A very broad absorption from about 2500 to 3000 cm-1 is the O-H stretch of a carboxylic acid.

Range to remember:
$$\text{O-H in } RCOOH \approx 2500-3000 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ (very broad)}$$

**Read the strong peak at 1710 cm-1**

A strong, sharp peak here means a carbonyl group. This is the C=O stretching vibration found in acids, esters, ketones and aldehydes.

Range to remember:
$$\text{C=O stretch} \approx 1680-1750 \text{ cm}^{-1} \text{ (strong, sharp)}$$

**Combine the two clues**

We need a molecule with both C=O and the carboxylic acid O-H. That combination is the $-COOH$ functional group.

Conclusion:
$$\text{C=O + broad O-H} = \text{carboxylic acid}$$

**Check the four names**

Propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, is the only carboxylic acid in the list, so it fits both peaks perfectly.

options.A: Methyl propanoate is an ester, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$. It has a C=O so it would show the 1710 cm-1 peak, but it has no O-H bond so it cannot show the broad 3000 cm-1 peak.
options.B: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. It has an O-H but no C=O, so it cannot show the strong 1710 cm-1 peak. Its alcohol O-H is also higher, around 3200-3600 cm-1, not the broad 2500-3000 cm-1 acid band.
options.C: Propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, contains both groups. Its C=O gives the strong peak at 1710 cm-1 and its hydrogen bonded acid O-H gives the very broad peak centred near 3000 cm-1. This matches both observations.
options.D: Propanone is a ketone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. It has a C=O so it would show the 1710 cm-1 peak, but it has no O-H bond at all, so the broad 3000 cm-1 peak would be missing.
